transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's the stairs, really — I keep getting out of breath going up to bed. I have to stop halfway and get my wind back.
When did you first notice this happening?
Oh, it's been going on a while back now. It's sort of crept up on me.
Do you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
No, I've never had any trouble with medicines, as far as I know.
How much is this getting in the way of your everyday life?
Well, it's not too bad most of the time, but it does hold me up. I'm slower than I used to be on the stairs.
Are you taking any medicines at all at the moment, whether they're ones you take regularly, ones you've just started, or ones you only take now and then?
Yes, I take a few tablets every day. My wife usually keeps track of them for me.
Have you ever been in hospital for anything?
I had a heart attack years back, and I've been in for that. I've also got a funny heartbeat — atrial fibrillation, they call it.
When you get out of breath going up the stairs to bed, is there anything else you notice at the same time?
Well, my ankles tend to get a bit puffy by the evening, and I've started using two pillows at night instead of one.
When you get out of breath going up the stairs, where do you feel it most, and does it spread anywhere else?
It's just breathlessness really — I don't get any pain with it, and nothing spreads anywhere. It's my breathing that's the trouble.
When you go up the stairs to bed, does the breathlessness happen every time, or only once in a while?
It's most times, I'd say, when I'm going up. If I take it slow I'm not too bad, but usually I have to stop.
What, if anything, worries you most about what's been happening?
I suppose I'm worried about whether my heart is getting worse, and how I'll manage the stairs to bed if it keeps up.
Besides the heart attack and the funny heartbeat you've told me about, is there anything else about your past health you'd like to add?
I did have a scan on my heart at the hospital last year, but I can't remember what they said about it. My wife might know better than me.
When the breathlessness comes on going up the stairs, is there anything else you notice at the same time that we haven't talked about yet?
No, I don't think so — no cough, no fever, nothing like that. Just the puffiness in my ankles and needing the extra pillow.
When did getting out of breath on the stairs first start for you — did it come on suddenly, build up gradually, or are you not sure?
It came on gradually, over about three months, I'd say. It wasn't sudden.

When you get out of breath on the stairs, how much does it affect you day to day — is it a mild nuisance, does it get in the way of things you'd like to do, does it stop you doing most things, or are you not sure?
It gets in the way a bit — I have to stop halfway up our fourteen stairs to catch my breath, and I never used to need to do that.
Besides the heart attack, the funny heartbeat, and the heart scan you mentioned, is there anything else about your health in the past that you’d like to add?
No, that's the lot as far as I remember. That's about all my health troubles.
When it comes to your medicines, are you mainly taking ones you've been on for a long time, ones you've started recently, or ones that have been changed recently, or are you not sure?
They're ones I've been on for a good while, I think. I've not had anything new started lately as far as I know.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
